solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: King not wanting vessel from the Netherlands

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
off can mean disinclined, as in being off one's food

explanation.surface: A monarch who has no wish for a Dutch boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A koff is a small two-masted Dutch sailing vessel, a Chambers word.

clue.text: Climber nipped by wingless fly complained

indicators.note: something nipped is gripped on both sides, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: the ked, or sheep-ked, is a wingless parasitic fly
vetch is a climbing plant of the pea family

explanation.surface: A climbing plant bitten by an insect moaned about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The climbing plant sits between the K and the ED of the fly.
explanation.definitionFit: To kvetch is Yiddish-derived slang for to whine or grumble persistently.

clue.text: Fine light fuse

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the lux is the SI unit of illumination

explanation.surface: A delicate fuse that gives off a little light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine light' reads as an adjective pair describing the fuse, but it splits into two pieces and fuse is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, flux means to melt or make fluid, a Chambers sense matching fuse.

clue.text: Grass turned up admitting need for bottle

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up makes it read from bottom to top
to admit is to let in, so the turned word takes something inside it

blocks.note: tef, or teff, is an Ethiopian cereal grass
a need is a lack

explanation.surface: Turned-up grass lets in a need for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link here, joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flacket is a Scots word for a flask or small bottle, listed in Chambers.

clue.text: Mistake is occurring twice in resetting of perm

indicators.note: resetting hair puts it in a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the word is taken two times
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hairdressing blunder: redoing a perm goes wrong twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Misprise, or misprize, is an archaic verb meaning to misunderstand or take wrongly.

clue.text: What waiters offer us after draughts?

indicators.note: after says which piece comes second when the two are joined end to end

blocks.note: the pieces in draughts (checkers) are called men
taken as written

explanation.surface: After a round of draught beer, the waiters bring us the bill of fare.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts suggests drinks or cold air; here it is the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiters hand diners the lists of dishes on offer, which are menus.

clue.text: Fishy perhaps, as in a cubist's doodle

indicators.note: a doodle is an aimless scribble, so these letters are jumbled
one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: qua is Latin for 'as', in the capacity of
the letters of a and cubist, the possessive ending dropped

explanation.surface: A modern painter's sketch looks rather fishy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is not a link but the Latin qua, placed inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish live underwater, so a fishy creature is an example of something subaquatic.

clue.text: Roller parking? Delay follows

indicators.note: follows puts the second piece after the first in the joined word

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
laten is a Chambers verb, to make later

explanation.surface: A driver asks about a car park space, then is told of a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A platen is the cylinder in a typewriter or press against which paper is held.

clue.text: Measure including old coin with money (6, two words)

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an inch is a unit of length
the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A sum including an antique coin, with cash on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in cash is an idiom for having funds available, so the phrase matches having money.

clue.text: Has wobbly movement? Not I! Not true if I've this

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and out of shape, so these letters are jumbled
says to take away a letter I from the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
kinesis is movement, especially of an organism

explanation.surface: Someone protests they are not the one who wobbles.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Is in the movement word goes. The definition plays on true meaning steady or level, as a wall is true.
explanation.definitionFit: True means straight and steady, so a person or thing with a tremor would not be true.

clue.text: Moved faster switching halves for advantage

indicators.note: swapping the front and back halves moves the opening letters round to the end

blocks.note: geed is past tense of gee, to urge a horse on

explanation.surface: A footballer speeded up and changed ends to gain the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a slight advantage over a rival, as in having the edge.

clue.text: See everybody, a clue solved, in the groove?

indicators.note: to solve a puzzle is to work it out, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: V is short for Latin vide, meaning see
all means everybody
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver delighted to have cracked a clue is in the groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the groove' sounds like an idiom for being on form; only 'groove' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vallecula is an anatomical or botanical furrow, a small groove or channel.

clue.text: Point in Ptolemaic system, as in variant of 10

indicators.note: a variant is a different form, so the letters are rearranged
one word goes within the other

blocks.note: qua is Latin for 'as'
the number written as a word

explanation.surface: An astronomy note cross-referring to the clue numbered 10.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 points not to the entry 10 across but simply to the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ptolemy's astronomy the equant is the point about which a planet's centre moves at uniform angular speed.

clue.text: Brie, rotten, going off? It's bright green and watery

indicators.note: food going off decays and breaks down, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A cheese gone bad has turned green and runny.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures mouldy cheese; the definition describes a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Torbernite is a hydrated copper uranium phosphate mineral forming bright green crystals, its water content making it watery.

clue.text: This horse I pen carelessly may be escaping

indicators.note: done carelessly, the letters of the named words are picked out from scattered places rather than together

blocks.note: the four letters to be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse in a corral may break out because I fenced it badly.
explanation.walkthrough: E, P, I and N are struck from the last word wherever they sit. Horse is slang for heroin, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scag and horse are both drug slang for heroin, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Love to stretch out, hot, inside cover, one of many to be seen in tea plantation? (9, two words)

definitions.text: one of many to be seen in tea plantation?

indicators.note: inside tells us the first three pieces sit within the following word

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, shaped like the letter O
to lie is to stretch out flat
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
a coat is a covering layer

explanation.surface: Someone loves to sprawl out, warm, under a blanket on an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link joining the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea pickers in Asia traditionally wear broad conical straw hats, so many such hats appear on a plantation.

clue.text: Cheese biscuit maybe Spooner's swallowed with fizzy pop?

indicators.note: Rev Spooner famously swapped sounds between words, so the sounds are exchanged

blocks.note: swallowed is ate and fizzy pop is Coke; swapping their vowel sounds

explanation.surface: A cheese cracker downed alongside a fizzy soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the swap is of vowel sounds, AY and OH, not opening consonants.
explanation.definitionFit: An oatcake is a flat oatmeal biscuit, often eaten with cheese, so it is an example.

clue.text: Packs up loaves

blocks.note: first meaning: breaks down or stops working
second meaning: heads, since loaf and conk are both slang for the head

explanation.walkthrough: Loaves looks like bread being packed; loaf is slang for head (use your loaf).
explanation.definitionFit: Conk is slang both for failing mechanically and for the head or nose.

clue.text: Red dye is one, when mixed

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A colourant turns out red when it is blended.
explanation.definitionFit: Eosin is a red fluorescent dye used to stain tissue in microscopy.

clue.text: One undressed may turn red with this – O!

definitions.text: One undressed may turn red with this – O!

indicators.note: turning into something else implies a change of form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words
taken as written, letters set aside
the letter itself, also set aside

explanation.surface: A person caught without clothes blushes at their state and cries out.
explanation.walkthrough: A compositional anagram: the letters of 'One undressed' equal RED plus the answer plus O, so remove RED and O to leave it. The whole clue also describes blushing at being naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undressed means being naked, the condition that makes someone blush.

clue.text: Poppet giving hint about somebody turned aside

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word encloses what follows
turned means the word immediately after it is read backwards

blocks.note: a hunch is an intuition or inkling
one means some person
by means aside, as in putting something by

explanation.surface: A sweetheart hints at somebody who has turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet and honeybunch are both affectionate terms for a darling, so synonyms.

clue.text: Electronic resistor? It's turned calmer with one installed

indicators.note: turned means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged
something installed is put in place within, so a letter is inserted

blocks.note: taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: A component that settles a circuit down becomes calmer once fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramal is a heat-resistant ceramic-metal composite (cermet), used for example in resistors; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Street ameer converted, brightly coloured with festoons

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
taken as written; an ameer is an emir
red is a bright colour

explanation.surface: A road where an emir has been converted is decked out in vivid bunting.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two words look like whole anagram fodder, but only 'ameer' is mixed; street is just ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Streamered means adorned with streamers, which are festoons or ribbons.

clue.text: Being dressed up in it makes one bristle

indicators.note: one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
trig means neat and smartly dressed

explanation.surface: Wearing smart clothes in this makes a person bristle with irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristle reads as a verb of annoyance, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A striga is a stiff bristle or hair-like scale on a plant, a botanical sense.

clue.text: Prone to sniffiness? John may make you this by the sound of it 6)

indicators.note: says the result is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: a john is slang for a toilet, which may be a urinal; urinal is heard as 'you' plus the answer

explanation.surface: A sniffy question about whether a lavatory makes you this.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has a stray '6)' printed in it. Say 'you' then the answer and you hear urinal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinal means relating to the nose, and a nose prone to sniffing is a rhinal matter, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Choir following words of old song stank

indicators.note: following places the second piece after the first

blocks.note: dit is an archaic word for a ditty or song words
ch is the abbreviation for choir

explanation.surface: A choir singing old-time lyrics smelled awful.
explanation.walkthrough: Stank is not the past tense of stink but a noun: a pond or ditch in Scots and dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: A stank is a dialect word for a pool or watercourse, matching a ditch.

clue.text: With which ballet-dancer kicks off jump?

definitions.text: With which ballet-dancer kicks off jump?

indicators.note: kicking off means starting, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter
a rise is an upward leap

explanation.surface: Asking what step a dancer uses to launch a leap.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a dancer kicks one leg off in this jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisé is a ballet jump in which the legs beat together in the air.

clue.text: Pro demanding money

blocks.note: first meaning: a prostitute
second meaning: cash, in British slang

explanation.walkthrough: Pro reads as a professional asking a fee; it is short for prostitute, called a brass in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is British slang for both cash and a prostitute.

clue.text: Victoria and suchlike showing expression at home with middle of reign

indicators.note: middle of means only the central letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: a term is a word or expression
in means at home
the central letter

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria shows a homely expression amid her reign.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria suggests the queen, whose reign fits; it is the London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is a London railway terminus, so stations like it are termini.

clue.text: Contraction gripping wife pressed from below

indicators.note: in a down entry, read from below means read bottom to top
gripping means holding inside, so one letter sits within

blocks.note: sat on, as when pressing down on something
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A labour pain holds a wife pushing from beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: Contraction suggests childbirth; it means a shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Twas is the shortened form of it was, so it is a contraction.

clue.text: Cadenzas perhaps, sensible if lacking depth

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: solid means sound or sensible
D is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: Showy cadenzas may be sensible but shallow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is a passage for the soloist alone, an example of solos or soli.

clue.text: Local spat now hidden (in part)

indicators.note: says the letters sit concealed inside part of the following words

blocks.note: spanning the end of now and the start of hidden

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood quarrel is now being kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue cheekily uses 'hidden' both as part of the hiding place and as its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, a whid is a quarrel or squabble, so local here means dialect.

clue.text: Sweet potato was served, 'eated inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

blocks.note: a dish came, or was served, to the table
hot with its H dropped, as the apostrophe signals

explanation.surface: The sweet potato was dished up, warmed through, in Cockney speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'eated marks the dropped H of heated.
explanation.definitionFit: Camote is a Spanish-derived name for the sweet potato.

clue.text: Fragrant additive – some rock's containing this, not half (9, two words)

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the first two of its four letters
containing means holding within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: basalt is a volcanic rock, made plural
the first half of the word

explanation.surface: A scented additive includes some crushed rock, not quite half of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath salts are scented crystals dissolved in bathwater, an additive for fragrance.

clue.text: Stone square round Vincent's home for a time – unlike his famous work?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first pair encloses what follows

blocks.note: st is the abbreviation for the stone, a British weight of 14 pounds
S as a short form of square
Van Gogh lived and painted in Arles in Provence

explanation.surface: A stone town square near where Van Gogh lived contrasts with his most famous painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Van Gogh's famous work is The Starry Night, so its opposite is a night without stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Starless means having no stars, the opposite of The Starry Night.

clue.text: Indication of some rock fan being bowled over?

indicators.note: something bowled over is knocked upside down, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a sail is a vane, as on a windmill, which acts as a fan

explanation.surface: A sign that a rock-music fan has been overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock and fan suggest music; lias is a geological term.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lias is a series of Lower Jurassic blue limestone and shale rocks.
